provider:claude.title: Claude
provider:claude.text: Uses the Claude plan you already pay for each month. Paying as you go with the Anthropic API is a separate choice.

provider:codex.title: ChatGPT / Codex
provider:codex.text: Signs in with your ChatGPT plan, the one you pay for each month. Pick it if you already use ChatGPT.

provider:antigravity.title: Google Antigravity
provider:antigravity.text: Uses your Antigravity plan. The Gemini API, billed by what you use, is a separate choice.

provider:cursor.title: Cursor
provider:cursor.text: Connects with an API key from your Cursor account: paste it into API key for Cursor, then choose Check key. The key stays in your computer's password store, never shown again.

provider:grok.title: Grok Build
provider:grok.text: Uses the Grok Build plan you pay for each month. The xAI API, billed by what you use, is a separate choice.

provider:muse.title: Muse Code
provider:muse.text: Uses the Muse Code plan you pay for each month. The Meta Model API, billed by what you use, is a separate choice.

provider:copilot.title: GitHub Copilot
provider:copilot.text: Signs in with the Copilot plan on your GitHub account. Pick it if you already pay for GitHub Copilot.

provider:qwen-coding.title: Qwen Coding Plan
provider:qwen-coding.text: Alibaba's monthly plan for coding with Qwen. It connects with a key from your Alibaba account.

provider:qwen-token.title: Qwen Token Plan
provider:qwen-token.text: Alibaba's Qwen plan that is billed by what you use, not by the month. It connects with a key from your Alibaba account.

provider:zai.title: Z.AI Coding Plan
provider:zai.text: Z.AI's monthly plan for coding. It connects with a key from your Z.AI account.

provider:kimi.title: Kimi Code
provider:kimi.text: Moonshot's monthly Kimi Code plan. It connects with a key from your Kimi account.

provider:minimax.title: MiniMax Coding Plan
provider:minimax.text: MiniMax's monthly plan for coding. It connects with a key from your MiniMax account.

provider:opencode-go.title: OpenCode Go
provider:opencode-go.text: OpenCode's monthly plan. It connects with a key from your OpenCode account.

provider:opencode-zen.title: OpenCode Zen
provider:opencode-zen.text: OpenCode's pay-as-you-go option, billed by what you use. It connects with a key from your OpenCode account.

provider:opencode-runtime.title: OpenCode on your computer
provider:opencode-runtime.text: Uses the OpenCode you already installed and set up yourself, with the accounts it already has. Pick it if OpenCode is how you work today.

provider:anthropic-api.title: Anthropic API
provider:anthropic-api.text: Pay as you go with Anthropic, billed by what you use. It is separate from a Claude plan and connects with a key.

provider:gemini-api.title: Gemini API
provider:gemini-api.text: Pay as you go with Google's Gemini, billed by what you use. It is separate from an Antigravity plan and connects with a key.

provider:vertex.title: Vertex AI
provider:vertex.text: Google's AI through your Google Cloud account, billed by Google Cloud. Pick it if your work already pays for Google Cloud.

provider:xai-api.title: xAI API
provider:xai-api.text: Pay as you go with xAI, billed by what you use. It is separate from a Grok Build plan and connects with a key.

provider:meta-api.title: Meta Model API
provider:meta-api.text: Pay as you go with Meta's models, billed by what you use. It is separate from a Muse Code plan and connects with a key.

pairing:approval.title: Approve from another device
pairing:approval.text: A device you already use with it shows a request, and you approve it there. The quickest way when that device is with you.

pairing:code.title: Enter the code it shows
pairing:code.text: Open your Puppet Master's page on the other computer, read the code it shows and type it here. Good when no other device is at hand.

pairing:qr.title: Scan its QR code
pairing:qr.text: Point this device's camera at the square code on the other screen. Handy on a phone or tablet.

field:headscale.title: Headscale address
field:headscale.text: The web address of your own Headscale server, starting with https://. Only for people who run Headscale instead of using a Tailscale account.

field:acc-bucket.title: Bucket
field:acc-bucket.text: The S3 or B2 bucket made for backups, like s3://my-backups. A bucket is storage space you rent from a cloud company.

field:acc-keyId.title: Access key ID
field:acc-keyId.text: The name that identifies this storage key. Copy it from your storage account; the separate secret access key is its password.

field:acc-secret.title: Secret access key
field:acc-secret.text: The private half of the bucket's key. Kept in your computer's password store, never in Puppet Master's files.

field:acc-address.title: Server address
field:acc-address.text: Where your backup server is. Start it with sftp:// for SFTP, or https:// for WebDAV.

field:acc-user.title: Username
field:acc-user.text: The name you sign in with on that backup server.

field:acc-password.title: Password
field:acc-password.text: The password for that backup server. Kept in your computer's password store, never in Puppet Master's files.

field:key.title: API key
field:key.text: A long secret code from the AI company that lets Puppet Master use your account. Paste it, then choose Check key. It stays in your computer's password store.

tour.title: Take the Guided Tour
tour.text: A few minutes, with a practice example, so nothing real changes. Pick it if Puppet Master is new to you.

enter.title: Enter Puppet Master
enter.text: Closes setup and opens Puppet Master now. You can start the Guided Tour any time from Settings.

startOver.title: Start over
startOver.text: Clears the choices from last time and begins setup again from the first page.

lookMenu.title: Change the look
lookMenu.text: Opens the looks right here, without leaving setup. Your choices so far are kept.

sound.title: Sound
sound.text: Turns setup's sounds and Pip's voice on or off. Nothing plays until you click or press a key.

close.title: Close
close.text: Your choices are saved. Finish setting up brings you back to where you left off.

resume.title: Finish setting up
resume.text: Opens setup again where you left off. Every choice you made is still there.

lookFamily:basic.title: Basic
lookFamily:basic.text: A clean diagram: plain shapes, calm and precise movement, quiet sounds. The calmest of the four.

lookFamily:friendly.title: Friendly
lookFamily:friendly.text: Warm colours, rounded shapes and playful movement, like a little paper theatre. The cosiest of the four.

lookFamily:glass.title: Glass
lookFamily:glass.text: Frosted glass over soft, moving light. Settings choose how see-through the panels are; text always stays readable.

lookFamily:retro.title: Retro
lookFamily:retro.text: Pixel-sharp, like an old computer. Dark is a glowing green screen; Light is printed on paper by a teletype.

lookMode:light.title: Light or dark
lookMode:light.text: Every look has a light and a dark version. First-time setup starts in Basic Dark; choose whichever is easier for you to read.

lookMode:dark.title: Light or dark
lookMode:dark.text: Every look has a light and a dark version. First-time setup starts in Basic Dark; choose whichever is easier for you to read.

lookNier:nier.title: NieR Mode
lookNier:nier.text: An ink-and-parchment look inspired by NieR: Automata. It paints over the look you pick; turn it off any time.

lookNierAdjust:nier-adjust.title: Adjust NieR look
lookNierAdjust:nier-adjust.text: Choose which parts of NieR Mode you want, like its menu sounds, its motion and the picture behind it. Works with NieR Mode on or off.

skipAll.title: Skip
skipAll.text: Closes setup and opens Puppet Master as it is. Run Onboarding Again in Settings brings setup back any time.

pickFamily:basic.title: Basic
pickFamily:basic.text: A clean diagram: plain shapes, calm and precise movement, quiet sounds. The calmest of the four.

pickFamily:friendly.title: Friendly
pickFamily:friendly.text: Warm colours, rounded shapes and playful movement, like a little paper theatre. The cosiest of the four.

pickFamily:glass.title: Glass
pickFamily:glass.text: Frosted glass over soft, moving light. Settings choose how see-through the panels are; text always stays readable.

pickFamily:retro.title: Retro
pickFamily:retro.text: Pixel-sharp, like an old computer. Dark is a glowing green screen; Light is printed on paper by a teletype.

group:pickMode.title: Light or dark
group:pickMode.text: Every look has a light and a dark version. First-time setup starts in Basic Dark; choose whichever is easier for you to read.

pickNier.title: NieR Mode
pickNier.text: An ink-and-parchment look inspired by NieR: Automata. It paints over the look you pick; turn it off any time.

adjustNier.title: Adjust NieR look
adjustNier.text: Choose which parts of NieR Mode you want, like its menu sounds, its motion and the picture behind it. Works with NieR Mode on or off.

pick:this.title: This computer
pick:this.text: Puppet Master does the work on this computer. You choose where its files and backups go in the next steps, and can add a Server later.

pick:connect.title: Connect this device
pick:connect.text: Already use Puppet Master on another computer? This device joins it and uses its Projects and AI. You confirm it is really you, once.

pick:server.title: Server
pick:server.text: The computer that does the work is called a Server. One that stays on, like a NAS, can keep working while your laptop sleeps.

restoreAll.title: Restore everything
restoreAll.text: For moving from an old computer: brings back your Projects, settings and look from a backup. Nothing here is replaced without asking.

group:pickServer.title: Found on your network
group:pickServer.text: Puppet Masters already running on your network. Pick the one this device should use; it shows how many Projects each one has.

field:addr.title: Its address
field:addr.text: The name or number other devices use to reach it, like home-nas.local or 192.168.1.20. Use it when yours is not in the list.

manualOn.title: Enter an address instead
manualOn.text: Type the address yourself when your Puppet Master does not show up on its own.

route:local_or_vpn.title: On this network
route:local_or_vpn.text: Finds it on the network you are on now. You can connect through a VPN too: Puppet Masters there show up as well.

route:tailscale.title: Tailscale
route:tailscale.text: Reach it from anywhere with Tailscale, a private network for your own devices. Pick it when you are away from home.

route:reverse_proxy.title: My own web address
route:reverse_proxy.text: For a Server its owner already put on a web address, like pm.example.com. Pick it only if you were given one.

route:remote_link.title: Puppet Master Remote Link
route:remote_link.text: A private link your Server can make for you. Paste the link it gave you; nothing else to set up.

tsControl:hosted.title: Tailscale account
tsControl:hosted.text: Sign in with an ordinary Tailscale account. Right for nearly everyone.

tsControl:headscale.title: My own Headscale server
tsControl:headscale.text: Headscale is a version of Tailscale you run yourself. Pick it only if you already have one.

field:proxy.title: Web address
field:proxy.text: The https:// address the Server owner set up, like https://pm.example.com.

field:link.title: Remote Link
field:link.text: The link your Server gave you, starting pm-remote-link:. Your Server shows it under Settings › Access.

field:code.title: Code from your Puppet Master
field:code.text: The 8 letters and numbers its page shows, like A7K9-M2Q4. It proves this device is with you.

resend.title: Send it again
resend.text: Asks the other device to show the request again, if you missed it or it went away.

createNew.title: Create a new Project
createNew.text: Starts a new Project on your Puppet Master, so it lives next to the work.

group:pickProject.title: Projects on your Puppet Master
group:pickProject.text: Projects it already has. Pick one to open first; every one of them is there for you later too.

kind:nas.title: A NAS or home server
kind:nas.text: A storage box or home server that stays on, like Synology, TrueNAS, Unraid or QNAP. A good home for a Server.

kind:cloud.title: A cloud computer
kind:cloud.text: A computer you rent online. It is always on and reachable, and costs a monthly fee from the company you rent it from.

kind:pc.title: Another computer
kind:pc.text: A Windows, Mac or Linux computer you leave switched on. Fine if it does not sleep.

group:platform.title: Install Puppet Master on it
group:platform.text: Pick what that computer runs, and follow its steps there. It shows up here by itself once it is running.

copy:install.title: Copy the install line
copy:install.text: Copies the line to paste into a terminal on that computer. A terminal is the window where you type commands.

group:guide.title: Open the install guide
group:guide.text: Opens the step-by-step guide for that system in your browser.

group:pick.title: Waiting to be set up
group:pick.text: A computer on your network running Puppet Master that is not set up yet. Choose it to make it your Server.

field:addr.title: Its address
field:addr.text: Where to reach it. A cloud computer does not show up on your home network, so enter the address its setup printed.

manualOn.title: Enter its address instead
manualOn.text: Type its address yourself if it does not appear on its own.

field:name.title: Name
field:name.text: What you'll call this Server everywhere in Puppet Master, like Home NAS. Pick a name you'll recognise.

group:suggest.title: Suggested names
group:suggest.text: A few names that fit this kind of computer. Pick one, or type your own.

field:code.title: Setup code
field:code.text: The number shown on the Server's own setup page, like 482 913. It proves the computer is yours.

selfMatch.title: The words match
selfMatch.text: Tick this only when the words here are the same as on this device. Nothing is paired until you approve.

newCode.title: New code
newCode.text: Makes a fresh code for adding a device. Devices already paired stay paired.

copy:pairlink.title: Copy the link
copy:pairlink.text: Copies a link another device on your network can open to join.

group:approve.title: Approve
group:approve.text: Lets that device use your Server. Approve only once its words match what the device shows.

group:deny.title: Deny
group:deny.text: Turns the request down. Nothing is shared with that device.

group:match.title: The words match
group:match.text: Compare the words with what the other device shows, then tick this. It unlocks Approve.

restore.title: Bring back old data
restore.text: Replacing an old Server? Brings its Projects back from a Recovery Kit or an old backup.

source:kit.title: A Recovery Kit file
source:kit.text: The file you saved when you set up backups. It knows where your backup is and how to open it. The best place to start.

source:folder.title: A folder on this computer
source:folder.text: A backup copied onto this computer, or on a drive you plugged in.

source:nas.title: A NAS or another computer
source:nas.text: A backup kept on a NAS or another computer. Puppet Master reaches it over a secure connection (SSH).

source:cloud.title: A cloud account
source:cloud.text: A backup kept in Google Drive, OneDrive, or an S3 or B2 bucket.

group:device.title: Which device
group:device.text: Devices on your network that can be reached securely. Pick the one that keeps the backup.

cloud:gdrive.title: Google Drive
cloud:gdrive.text: You sign in to Google on its own page next. Puppet Master only reads the backup.

cloud:onedrive.title: OneDrive
cloud:onedrive.text: You sign in to Microsoft on its own page next. Puppet Master only reads the backup.

cloud:s3.title: S3 or B2
cloud:s3.text: A cloud storage bucket. Fill in its three access details below to reach it.

field:phrase.title: Recovery phrase
field:phrase.text: The six words in your Recovery Kit, like river candle orbit maple quiet lantern. Used once and never saved.

group:pick.title: Choose what to bring back
group:pick.text: Each copy is a moment the backup was taken. The newest is usually the right one.

group:pickProject.title: Your Projects
group:pickProject.text: Everything that came back. Pick the one to open first.

createNew.title: Create a new Project
createNew.text: Starts something new instead. Your restored Projects are all still there.

pick:new.title: New Project
pick:new.text: Puppet Master makes an empty folder for it and saves every version from the very first file.

pick:existing.title: Existing work
pick:existing.text: A folder on this computer, a Project stored online like GitHub, or files on another device. Puppet Master reads it but changes nothing until you create the Project.

pick:restore.title: Restore
pick:restore.text: Brings a Project back from one of your backups.

sub:folder.title: A folder on this computer
sub:folder.text: Work already in a folder on the computer doing the work. Pick the folder next; it is only read until you create the Project.

sub:online.title: A Project stored online
sub:online.text: Work kept on a website like GitHub or GitLab. Sign in and pick it; the next steps show where your working copy will live.

sub:device.title: Files on another device
sub:device.text: Work on a NAS, a network drive or another computer. Puppet Master works on it right where it is.

later.title: Set up a Project later
later.text: No Project is created now; make one whenever you like. Setup finishes without one.

group:pick.title: Recent folders
group:pick.text: Folders you used lately. Puppet Master reads the one you pick but changes nothing until you create the Project.

browse.title: Browse
browse.text: Look through your folders and choose any one, if it is not in the list.

group:treeGo.title: Choose a folder
group:treeGo.text: Open folders to look inside. When you are in the right one, use Choose this folder.

field:name.title: Project name
field:name.text: The name shown for this Project in Puppet Master. For a new Project it also names its folder. An existing folder keeps its own name and place.

group:suggest.title: Suggestions
group:suggest.text: A few example names to start from. Pick one, then change any word you like.

change.title: Where its files live
change.text: Shows where the folder will be kept. Change picks another folder here, or a network drive.

loc:auto.title: On this computer
loc:auto.text: In Puppet Master's own folder in Documents. Easy to find, and right for most people.

loc:custom.title: Another folder on this computer
loc:custom.text: Keep it in a folder you choose, like one you already use for this kind of work.

loc:network.title: A network drive or NAS
loc:network.text: Keep the files on a storage device on your network. Uses a secure connection (SSH) by default.

field:custom.title: Choose a folder
field:custom.text: The folder path to use, like ~/Documents/Clubs. The ~ means your own home folder.

storage:with_server.title: On your Server
storage:with_server.text: Recommended. The Server keeps the files next to the work, so nothing waits on this device.

storage:this_device.title: On this device
storage:this_device.text: Files stay on this device and the Server reaches them over the network. This device needs to be on while it works.

storage:network_location.title: A network drive
storage:network_location.text: A NAS or shared folder on your network keeps the files, and the Server works on them there.

pick:fresh.title: Start fresh
pick:fresh.text: Puppet Master's standard settings. Right for a first Project, or when you want a clean start.

group:pick.title: Like another Project
group:pick.text: Reuses the settings of a Project you already trust. Never copied: sign-ins and keys, files, history, Goals and Plans.

choose.title: Choose settings
choose.text: Pick which groups of settings come along, like look, notifications or AI accounts.

group:cat.title: Settings to copy
group:cat.text: Each group is a set of settings from that Project. Switch one off to keep the standard ones for it.

pick:github.title: GitHub
pick:github.text: GitHub is a free website that keeps an online copy of your work. The most popular, and free for private Projects.

pick:gitlab.title: GitLab
pick:gitlab.text: A website like GitHub. Pick it if you or your team already use GitLab, on gitlab.com or your own server.

pick:azure_devops.title: Azure DevOps
pick:azure_devops.text: Microsoft's service for teams. Pick it if your work already keeps Projects in Azure DevOps.

pick:bitbucket_cloud.title: Bitbucket
pick:bitbucket_cloud.text: Atlassian's website for keeping work online. Pick it if your team uses Bitbucket.

pick:forgejo.title: Forgejo
pick:forgejo.text: A free service you can run on your own server, or use on Codeberg. Pick it if you already have one.

pick:gitea.title: Gitea
pick:gitea.text: A small service you can run on your own server, or use as Gitea Cloud. Pick it if you already have one.

pick:github_enterprise.title: GitHub Enterprise
pick:github_enterprise.text: GitHub run on your company's own server. Pick it if your company gave you its address.

pick:cursor_origin.title: Cursor Origin
pick:cursor_origin.text: Cursor's own service for keeping work online. It is still a preview, so expect changes.

notNow.title: Not now
notNow.text: Leaves out the online copy for now. Safe History still keeps your versions; add an online copy later.

group:variant.title: Which edition
group:variant.text: The same service, run by the company itself or on your own server. Pick the one your account is on.

field:address.title: Server address
field:address.text: Where your own copy of the service lives, starting with https://, like https://git.example.com.

group:useKnown.title: Use this account
group:useKnown.text: This computer is already signed in to it. Puppet Master only asks for access to the Project you choose.

another.title: Use a different account
another.text: Sign in with another account instead, like a work one.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.text: Opens its sign-in page in your browser. Sign in there, then come back; nothing else to type here.

create.title: Create account
create.text: No account yet? Opens its sign-up page. Make the account there, then sign in here.

tokenOn.title: Use an access token instead
tokenOn.text: A token is a long password made just for apps. Use it when your server does not offer browser sign-in.

field:token.title: Access token
field:token.text: Make one on your server under Settings › Applications. It stays in your computer's password store, never in Puppet Master's files.

code.title: Browser didn't open?
code.text: Shows a short code instead. Open the address it gives on any device and type the code there.

copyLink.title: Browser didn't open?
copyLink.text: Copies the sign-in link, so you can paste it into your browser yourself.

copy:dcode.title: Copy the code
copy:dcode.text: Copies this sign-in code. Paste it on the page named above.

newCode.title: New code
newCode.text: Makes a fresh code if this one ran out. Codes last 15 minutes.

signupBack.title: Back to sign in
signupBack.text: Made your account on its page? Choose this, then sign in with it.

field:repo.title: Name on the service
field:repo.text: How the online copy appears there. The suggestion is fine; letters, numbers and dashes work best.

group:owner.title: Whose account keeps it
group:owner.text: Your own account, or an organization you belong to. Pick an organization when the Project belongs to a team.

group:azOrg.title: Organization
group:azOrg.text: The Azure DevOps organization the Project belongs to.

group:azProject.title: Team project
group:azProject.text: Azure DevOps groups work into team projects. Pick one marked Git, the kind used for code. This is separate from your Puppet Master Project.

azRefresh.title: Refresh projects
azRefresh.text: Looks again for team projects, like one you just made on Azure DevOps.

azCreateTeamProject.title: Create a team project
azCreateTeamProject.text: Opens Azure DevOps to make a new team project there. Come back and refresh to pick it.

vis:private.title: Only you
vis:private.text: Only you, and people you invite, can see it. Right for most Projects.

vis:public.title: Everyone
vis:public.text: Anyone on the internet can see it; only you and people you invite can change it. Pick it for work you want to share.

vis:internal.title: Everyone in your organization
vis:internal.text: People in your organization can see it; nobody outside can.

field:desc.title: Description
field:desc.text: A sentence about the Project, shown on its online page. Optional.

field:branch.title: Main branch name
field:branch.text: The name of the main line of your work, usually main. Leave it unless your team uses another name.

readme.title: Add a README file
readme.text: A short page that says what the Project is. It is the first thing people see online.

group:gitignore.title: Files to leave out
group:gitignore.text: Some files, like temporary ones, should never be copied online. Chosen for you works for nearly everyone.

group:license.title: License
group:license.text: Says what others may do with your work if you share it. No license keeps all rights with you.

field:q.title: Search your Projects
field:q.text: Type part of a name to find it quickly.

group:pick.title: Choose the Project
group:pick.text: Only the Project you pick is copied. The line below shows where the working copy will be kept.

group:backend.title: Git or Jujutsu
group:backend.text: Both keep saved versions of your Project without an account. Git is the usual choice; Jujutsu works with Git and makes mistakes easier to undo.

backend:git.title: Git
backend:git.text: Git is the most common way to keep versions. Recommended. Works with GitHub and every other online service.

backend:jujutsu.title: Jujutsu
backend:jujutsu.text: A newer tool built on Git. Mistakes are easier to undo, and it still works with GitHub and the others.

filesafe.title: FileSafe
filesafe.text: Keeps a safety copy of each file before big changes. An extra layer on top of Safe History.

online.title: Online copy
online.text: A copy on a website like GitHub. You choose who can see it. Puppet Master only asks for access to the Project you choose.

backup.title: Backup
backup.text: A full copy you can restore from, kept somewhere else: a Home NAS over your home network, Google Drive, OneDrive, or another server.

bdest:nas.title: Home NAS
bdest:nas.text: A storage box on your home network keeps the backup. Close by and quick.

bdest:gdrive.title: Google Drive
bdest:gdrive.text: Keeps the backup in your Google account. You'll sign in right after your Project is created.

bdest:onedrive.title: OneDrive
bdest:onedrive.text: Keeps the backup in your Microsoft account. You'll sign in right after your Project is created.

bdest:s3.title: S3 or B2
bdest:s3.text: A cloud storage bucket you rent. Good if you already have one; you add its access details after your Project is created.

bdest:sftp.title: Another server
bdest:sftp.text: A server you can reach over SFTP or WebDAV keeps the backup, like one at work or a friend's.

bdest:none.title: Not now
bdest:none.text: No separate backup for now. Safe History still keeps versions with your Project; add a backup later in Settings.

pick:home.title: Only at home
pick:home.text: Your devices reach the Server on your home network, or on a private network you already use, called a VPN.

pick:anywhere.title: Away from home
pick:anywhere.text: Tailscale connects your devices through a private network. Sign in once to reach your Server while you are away from home.

route:headscale.title: My own Headscale server
route:headscale.text: Like Tailscale, but run on a server of your own. Pick it only if you already run Headscale.

route:reverse_proxy.title: My own web address
route:reverse_proxy.text: Puts it on a web address you own, like pm.example.com. Puppet Master sets up Caddy with a free certificate.

route:remote_link.title: Puppet Master Remote Link
route:remote_link.text: Puppet Master carries the connection between your devices. Use its private link without changing your network settings.

field:proxy.title: Web address
field:proxy.text: The address you own and want to use, starting with https://, like https://pm.example.com.

hosting:generate_for_server.title: Puppet Master sets it up
hosting:generate_for_server.text: Puppet Master sets up the proxy (the program that answers on that address) for you. The easiest way.

hosting:generate_only.title: Only make the settings file
hosting:generate_only.text: You get the file to use with a proxy you set up yourself. For people who manage their own.

hosting:existing_proxy.title: I already have one
hosting:existing_proxy.text: Your address already points at a proxy you run. Puppet Master just uses it.

tls:lets_encrypt.title: A free certificate
tls:lets_encrypt.text: The certificate makes the address safe to use (the padlock in your browser). A free one renews by itself.

tls:existing_certificate.title: My own certificate
tls:existing_certificate.text: Use a certificate you already have for that address.

group:kind.title: Which proxy
group:kind.text: Caddy is the default. NGINX, Traefik and Nginx Proxy Manager are also supported. Pick the one you already use.

field:link.title: Remote Link
field:link.text: Paste the Remote Link here. Your Server shows it under Settings › Access.

group:edit.title: Edit
group:edit.text: Goes back to change this choice. Your Project hasn't been created yet.

retry.title: Try again
retry.text: Tries the unfinished step again. Work that already finished is kept.

rename.title: Change the name
rename.text: Pick another name for the online copy, since that one is already used there.

skipOnline.title: Skip the online copy
skipOnline.text: Finish without the online copy. You can add one later from Settings.

askSkip.title: Skip the online copy
askSkip.text: Finish without the online copy. You can add one later from Settings.

confirmDelete.title: Delete the online copy
confirmDelete.text: Deletes only the online copy named here. This can't be undone; your files here are kept.

cancelDelete.title: Keep it
cancelDelete.text: Keeps the online copy and returns to the recovery choices.

continueSetup.title: Continue Setup
continueSetup.text: Picks up the setup where it stopped, using the online copy that was already made.

openRepo.title: Open the online copy
openRepo.text: Opens the online copy on its website, so you can see what was made.

deleteRepo.title: Delete the online copy
deleteRepo.text: Deletes only the online copy, and can't be undone. Your files here are not touched.

checkAgain.title: Check again
checkAgain.text: Asks the service again how the setup went. Nothing is retried or deleted on its own.

reviewAgain.title: Review setup again
reviewAgain.text: Goes back to the review to start a fresh attempt. The old one is never reused.

step:signin.title: Sign in or connect
step:signin.text: Lets Puppet Master reach the place your backups go. You do it once.

step:test.title: Run a quick test
step:test.text: Makes a small backup and reads it back, to prove it works before you rely on it.

step:kit.title: Save your Recovery Kit
step:kit.text: The Recovery Kit is the only way back in if this computer is lost. Keep it somewhere safe, like a password manager.

step:kitTest.title: Check your Recovery Kit
step:kitTest.text: Opens the backup with the kit you saved, so you know it is the right one before you need it.

step:policy.title: Turn on daily backups
step:policy.text: Turns on an automatic backup each night, while the computer doing the work and the backup place are available.

stepUp.title: Confirm it's you
stepUp.text: The kit is shown only to you, once, on this device. This makes sure it is really you asking.

later.title: Do this later
later.text: Your Project is ready either way. Backups wait until you finish these steps.

all.title: See all providers
all.text: Every AI Puppet Master works with, in two groups: monthly plans and pay-as-you-go accounts.

none.title: I don't have any of these
none.text: No AI account yet? Shows the kinds there are, so you can pick one that suits you.

skip.title: Skip for now
skip.text: Puppet Master can't plan or work until an AI is added. Add one any time from Settings.

free.title: Set Up Free Models
free.text: Add free options for suitable tasks. Availability and limits can vary, and your paid accounts are used first.

group:install.title: Install
group:install.text: This AI needs its own app on the computer that does the work. Puppet Master uses the maker's official installer.

field:q.title: Search
field:q.text: Type a name, like Claude, Gemini or OpenCode, to find it quickly.

pick:sub.title: A monthly plan
pick:sub.text: Like Claude or ChatGPT. One price each month, and the simplest place to start.

pick:api.title: Pay as you go
pick:api.text: Like the Anthropic or Gemini API. You pay for what you use, which suits light or occasional use.

pick:free.title: Free Models
pick:free.text: Free options with limits. Good for trying things out before you pay for anything.

group:signup.title: Sign-up pages
group:signup.text: Opens that company's own sign-up page in your browser. Come back here once you have an account.

route:free-openrouter.title: OpenRouter free models
route:free-openrouter.text: A site that offers several AI models for free, with limits. You sign in on its page.

route:free-github-models.title: GitHub Models
route:free-github-models.text: Free AI from GitHub, with limits. Uses your GitHub account, so it is ready by itself once you sign in to GitHub here.

route:free-cerebras.title: Cerebras free tier
route:free-cerebras.text: Cerebras's free option, known for quick answers. Limits apply.

route:free-groq.title: Groq free tier
route:free-groq.text: Groq's free option. It is popular, so it can be busy for a while.

route:free-hf.title: Hugging Face Inference
route:free-hf.text: Free AI from Hugging Face, a big library of models. Limits apply.

attribution.title: Where this list comes from
attribution.text: The free model list is based on a community list. Opens it in your browser.

summary:free.title: Free Models
summary:free.text: Free options with limits, good for trying things out. Your paid accounts are always used first.

summary:backup.title: Backup
summary:backup.text: A full copy of your Project kept somewhere else. Not set up yet? Add one any time in Settings.

createNow.title: Create a Project now
createNow.text: Goes back to make your first Project now. What you already set up stays as it is.

method:ssh.title: SSH
method:ssh.text: Recommended. A secure way to reach the device. Puppet Master uses a key, so no password is kept.

method:smb.title: SMB
method:smb.text: Windows and Mac file sharing. Pick it for a shared folder you already open from your computer.

method:nfs.title: NFS
method:nfs.text: File sharing many NAS devices and Linux computers use. Pick it if your device shares that way.

method:mounted.title: Already connected
method:mounted.text: A drive this computer already shows in its file browser. Nothing more to connect.

group:device.title: Choose a device
group:device.text: Devices Puppet Master found on your network. Nothing is changed by looking.

field:addr.title: Address
field:addr.text: Where to reach the device, like 192.168.1.20 or nas.local.

field:port.title: Port
field:port.text: The door number SSH answers on. Leave it at 22 unless whoever set up the device changed it.

manualOn.title: Type an address instead
manualOn.text: Enter its address yourself if the device does not show up.

group:share.title: Shared folders found
group:share.text: Folders the device shares on your network. Pick the one with the files.

group:volume.title: Connected drives
group:volume.text: Drives this computer already shows in its file browser.

trust.title: Yes, this is my device
trust.text: Every device has its own picture. Choose this when it matches what your device shows in its settings.

trustNew.title: Trust the new ID
trustNew.text: Only if you reset the device yourself. Otherwise something may be pretending to be it, so stop.

stop.title: Stop
stop.text: Stops here and connects to nothing. The safe choice when you didn't reset the device.

group:pick.title: Choose a key
group:pick.text: A key lets Puppet Master connect without a password. These are on the computer that will connect; only the part safe to share is read.

pick:new.title: Make a new key
pick:new.text: A key just for Puppet Master. Easy to remove later, and it doesn't touch your other keys.

field:pass.title: Passphrase
field:pass.text: The password that locks this key. It unlocks the key on this computer and isn't saved.

field:user.title: Username
field:user.text: The name you use for the device's web page.

field:pw.title: Password
field:pw.text: Used once to add your key. Never saved. After this, no password is needed.

selfOn.title: I'll add the key myself
selfOn.text: Shows the line to add to the device yourself, so you never type your password here.

selfOff.title: Add it for me
selfOff.text: Puppet Master adds the key for you with your password, used once and never saved.

copy:pub.title: Copy the key line
copy:pub.text: Copies the public half of your key, the part that is safe to share, to add on the device.

fixPerms.title: Fix the folder permissions
fixPerms.text: The device refused the key because its home folder is shared too widely. This tightens it so the key works.

useSsh.title: Use SSH instead
useSsh.text: Connect with a key instead of pairing. Only needed if you would rather not pair with its Puppet Master.

another.title: Choose another way
another.text: Pick a different way to approve this computer, like a code instead of a request.

field:pmcode.title: Code from the device
field:pmcode.text: The 8 letters and numbers its Puppet Master shows, like A7K9-M2Q4.

resend.title: Send it again
resend.text: Asks for the request to be shown again, if you missed it.

group:cd.title: Choose a folder
group:cd.text: Open folders to find the right one. Read-only folders cannot hold a Project.

adding.title: New folder
adding.text: Makes a fresh folder for the Project. It is made when you create the Project.

field:newName.title: Folder name
field:newName.text: A name for the new folder, like the Project name.

field:user.title: Username
field:user.text: The name you use for the shared folder. Your sign-in stays in your computer's password store.

field:pw.title: Password
field:pw.text: The password for the shared folder. It stays in your computer's password store, not in Puppet Master.

group:volume.title: Choose the drive
group:volume.text: Drives this computer already shows in its file browser. Pick the one that holds the Project.

welcome.resumed: You're back! I kept your place.
welcome.returning: Welcome back. I found your things.

look.enter: Dress me up. It changes everything.
look.keep: Your look's kept. Change it if you like.
look.pickFamily:friendly: Soft and cosy. I like it.
look.pickFamily:glass: Ooh, shiny. Am I glass now?
look.pickFamily:retro: Retro! Straight out of an old computer.
look.pickMode:light: Light it is. Bright and clear.

where.enter: Where shall we do the work?
where.pick:server: A server never sleeps. Lucky thing.
where.offline: No internet? Local work still works.

c-route.group:pickServer: That one? I'll string us together.
c-route.route:remote_link: A Remote Link? Paste it in.
c-route.typing: Type it in. I'll go and knock.

c-review.enter: It'll ask if it's really you.
c-review.pairing:approval: Tap approve on your other device.
c-review.pairing:code: A code! I love a secret.
c-review.pairing:qr: Say cheese to the QR code!

c-pair.waiting: Waiting for your OK over there…
c-pair.typing: Ooh, a code. Read it carefully.

c-ready.enter: Connected! Open one, or start fresh.
c-ready.empty: No Projects there yet. Make the first!
c-ready.createNew: Something new? I'll fetch a page.
c-ready.group:pickProject: Ooh, that one. Shall we open it?

s-kind.enter: What kind of computer will it be?
s-kind.kind:nas: A NAS! It never takes a nap.
s-kind.kind:cloud: A computer in the clouds. Ooh.
s-kind.kind:pc: Another computer that stays on. Handy.

s-wait.enter: Waiting for it to show up…
s-wait.found: There it is! Shall we set it up?
s-wait.typing: An address! I'll go and look.

s-confirm.enter: Give it a name you'll know.
s-confirm.typing: Ooh, what shall we call it?
s-confirm.selfMatch: Same words? Then tick the box.

s-ready.enter: Your Server is ready! Bring friends.
s-ready.waiting: Someone wants in. Check the words.

r-source.source:kit: The Recovery Kit! The very best key.
r-source.source:folder: A folder, or a drive you plugged in.
r-source.source:nas: On the NAS? I'll go and fetch it.
r-source.source:cloud: Up in the cloud. I'll bring it down.
r-source.typing: Ooh, bucket details. I'll be careful.

r-unlock.typing: A secret phrase. I won't keep it.

r-pick.enter: Which copy shall we bring back?
r-pick.group:pick: That one? Newest is usually best.

r-preview.done: All back, just as it was.

begin.server: We'll keep it next to the work.
begin.pick:existing: Bring it in. I'll learn my way round.
begin.pick:restore: Back from the archive, good as new.
begin.sub:folder: A folder you already have. Easy.
begin.sub:device: On another device? I'll go and look.

ex-folder.hasHistory: It keeps its own history. Neat!
ex-folder.noHistory: No history yet. I'll start one.

name.storage:with_server: Right next to the work. Smart.
name.storage:network_location: On a shared drive. Got it.

like.enter: Copy a Project you already trust?
like.group:pick: Same setup as that one? Smart.

online-service.pick:gitlab: GitLab. A good home for it.
online-service.pick:forgejo: Forgejo. Where shall we find yours?

online-signin.enter: Sign in. I'll only ask for this one.
online-signin.known: You're signed in already. Use it?
online-signin.waiting: Over to your browser. I'll wait.
online-signin.typing: Ooh, a token. Into the keychain.
online-signin.create: Make your account, then come back!

online-details.typing: Ooh, a name for the copy.
online-details.vis:private: Just you, and who you invite.

ex-repos.group:pick: That one? I'll copy it over.
ex-repos.empty: Hmm, I can't see any here.

safe.enter: Every version goes in the vault.
safe.backend:git: Git keeps track of your changes.
safe.install: I'll install it while we build.
safe.keeps: It keeps its own history. Good.
safe.filesafe: An extra safety copy before big changes.
safe.online: A copy in the cloud, just in case.
safe.bdest:nas: On your home NAS. Close by.
safe.bdest:s3: A bucket! I love a bucket.
safe.sync: Your other devices will see it too.

away.enter: Should it answer when you're out?
away.pick:home: Home it is. I'll keep the lights on.
away.route:remote_link: A private link through the relay.

review.checked: All checked. Ready when you are.
review.later: Nothing gets made yet. That's fine.

creating.doneLater: All set up. A Project can wait.
creating.closeOk: Close me if you like. I'll keep going.

protect.enter: Let's finish setting up your backup.
protect.step:kitTest: Let's be sure the kit opens it.

ai.signingIn: Over to your browser. I'll wait.
ai.typing: Ooh, a key. I'll keep it secret.
ai.free: Free models? Good for a start.

ai-all.enter: Every AI I can work with.
ai-all.typing: Ooh, who are we looking for?

ai-none.pick:api: Pay for what you use. Fair.

ready.later: All set. Make a Project whenever!

nas-find.sshOff: Flip SSH on, and I'll try again.
nas-find.pm: It runs Puppet Master too! No keys.
nas-find.typing: An address! I'll go and knock.

nas-identity.enter: Is this your device? Check its picture.

nas-key.group:pick: That key? Let's see what it needs.
nas-key.notAdded: That key isn't on it yet. I'll add it.
nas-key.pick:new: A brand-new key, just for me!

nas-signin.enter: Just once, to add your key.
nas-signin.self: Add this line, then tell me.

nas-pmpair.waiting: Waiting for the OK over there…
nas-pmpair.typing: Ooh, a code. Read it carefully.

nas-smb.enter: Sign in to the shared folder.

name.long: That won't fit on my sign!
name.exists: Oh! You already have one called that.

missing.name: A name first, please!
missing.signin: Sign in first, then on we go.
missing.azureProject: Pick the Azure DevOps project first.
missing.remoteLink: I need the Remote Link first.
missing.proxyAddress: I need your web address first.

route.none: Hmm, I can't find it yet.

pair.expired: Oh, that request ran out of time.

confirm.ownerFail: The Server turned that step down.
confirm.evidenceMissing: I couldn't confirm that step finished.
confirm.pendingHost: No answer from the Server yet…

ready.staleReq: That request used the old code.
ready.staleAdopt: That answer was for an old code.
ready.wrongTarget: That answer was meant for someone else!
ready.codeMissing: We need a new code first.
ready.wordsMissing: I can't see its words. Ask again?

unlock.wrong: Hmm, those words don't unlock it.

protect.accessMissing: I need all three to connect.
protect.testFailed: That kit didn't open the backup.

find.stillOff: SSH is still switched off there.

key.old: That key is too old. Choose another.

signin.lockout: Careful, it may lock us out.

fail.refused: It refused the key. Folder trouble.
fail.not_allowed: This account can't use SSH there.
fail.not_added: The key isn't on it yet.

folder.readOnly: I can't write in that folder.

signin.admin: Sign-ups are off on that server.
signin.fail: Oh no. That sign-in didn't finish.

backup.nasSame: A backup there wouldn't be safe.

review.backupDropped: I took that backup off. Pick again?

recovery.notice: It's half made. Let's finish it.
recovery.failedLead: Nothing was made yet. Try again?
recovery.unknown: I'm not sure how that went yet.

reasons.claimBusy: Another setup is still running. I'll wait.
reasons.deleteGated: The service must confirm before deleting.
reasons.noBinding: No confirmed online copy to open yet.
reasons.noRemote: No online copy has been confirmed yet.
reasons.stale: That answer was for the earlier setup.
reasons.mismatch: That answer doesn't match this setup.
reasons.confirmFirst: Check which online copy to delete first.
reasons.openUnavailable: I can't open that in this preview.
reasons.other: That isn't available yet. Nothing changed.

nier.missing: Those choices aren't available here yet.

ai.signinFail: Oh no. That sign-in didn't go through.
ai.skipNote: No AI yet, so I'll nap. Add one later.
ai.unavailable: That account isn't here. Sign in again?

like.unavailable: That account isn't on this computer.

free.limited: That one's busy right now. Too popular!

protect.testFailed: The kit works! Keep it safe.

find.stillOff: SSH is on! Off we go.

signin.selfNot: Found it! The key is in.

oopsAny.screen: Oops. The note says what to do next.
oopsAny.field: Oops. That entry needs another look.

signinFail.title: Didn't sign in
signinFail.body: The sign-in on {vendor}'s page didn't finish, so nothing was connected. Try again, and finish signing in there.

fail.title: Didn't sign in
fail.body: The sign-in on {name}'s page didn't finish, so nothing was shared. Try again, and finish signing in there.

signin.createLead: Finish making your account on {name}'s own page. Setup never asks for your sign-up details.

azure.create: Create a team project on Azure DevOps
azure.routeMissing: A team project can't be made from here for this Server. Pick an existing Git project after Refresh projects, or skip the online copy.
azure.createNote: The team project is made on Azure DevOps itself. Come back and choose Refresh projects; only a finished Git project can be picked.
azure.signinFirst: Sign in to this Azure DevOps first, then refresh the projects.

creating.settingsPublishError: Your Project is kept. Its settings still need to finish before it can open. Check again retries only that last step; nothing else is made again.

meetPip.title: Meet Pip.
meetPip.body: Pip is every agent Puppet Master directs, and you hold the strings. It will walk you through setup.

meetCrew.title: Meet the crew.
meetCrew.body: When Puppet Master runs a Plan, every agent is a Pip in its role's hat: the Coordinator's crown, the Builder's hard hat, the Reviewer's glasses.
